chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

Al-Makhzūmī narrated to me—and his mother was from the descendants of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام). He said: Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) sent for us, so he gathered us and then said to us, “Do you know why I invited you?” We said, “No.”

So he said: “Bear witness that this son of mine is my waṣī, the one who will undertake my affair, and my khalīfah after me. Whoever has a debt owed by me, let him take it from this son of mine. Whoever has been promised something by me, let him have it fulfilled through him. And whoever has no alternative but to meet me, then let him not meet me except with his letter.”

key_terms.الْقَيِّمُ بِأَمْرِي: the one who will manage and uphold my affairs
key_terms.بِكِتَابِهِ: with his written authorization or letter
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed and to be repaid
key_terms.عِدَةٌ: a promise or commitment due for fulfillment

ai.seo_question: How did Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) designate Imām al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) as his successor?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) publicly identifying his son as his waṣī, the one responsible for his affairs, and his khalīfah after him. It also shows the transfer of practical and financial responsibilities to him, indicating recognized religious authority and succession.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said,

‘Al-Makhzoumy narrated to me, and it was so that his paternal uncle was from the children of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>. He said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> sent for me. So we gathered ourselves, then said to us: ‘Do you know why I<sup>asws</sup> invited you all?’ So we said, ‘No’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Bear witness that this son<sup>asws</sup> of mine<sup>asws</sup> is my<sup>asws</sup> successor<sup>asws</sup>, and the establisher of my<sup>asws</sup> commands, and my<sup>asws</sup> Caliph after me<sup>asws</sup>. The one who has a debt for him with me<sup>asws</sup>, so let him take it from this son<sup>asws</sup> of mine<sup>asws</sup>, and the one who had a promise for him with me<sup>asws</sup>, so let him have it fulfilled from him<sup>asws</sup>, and the one for whom it is inevitable that he must meet me<sup>asws</sup>, so he should not come to meet me<sup>asws</sup> except by his<sup>asws</sup> letter (Written authorisation)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Fudayl who has said that al-Makhdhumi whose mother was one of the children of Ja‘far ibn abu Talib has narrated the following.
“Abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) once called all of us to see him. We all gathered and then he said to us, “Do you know why have I called you?” We said, “We do not know.”

He then said, “Bear testimony that this my son is the executor of my will, the director of my affairs and the succeeding Imam (a.s.). Whoever has a loan due on me should demand from my son, this one. To whoever I may have promised anything should also acquire from him. Whoever must see me must not come to see me with writing from him.”
